Lemma
[the geodesic equation is chart-independent]

↗ def:dc-ch3-2-1 ↗ lem:dc-ch7-2-8-christoffel-transform

1. ch7:2.8Let $\gamma $ be a curve in $M$ continuous at $t_0$ whose foot $\gamma (t_0)$ lies in the domains of two charts $\varphi _\alpha ,\varphi _\beta $, and write $u_\alpha =\varphi _\alpha \circ \gamma $, $u_\beta =\varphi _\beta \circ \gamma $. If $u_\alpha $ is differentiable near $t_0$, its derivative is differentiable at $t_0$, and the second-order geodesic equation $u_\alpha ''+\Gamma ^\alpha (u_\alpha ',u_\alpha ')(u_\alpha )=0$ holds at $t_0$, then the same three statements hold for $u_\beta $. In particular the geodesic equation of section def:dc-ch3-2-1, read in the chart at the moving foot $\gamma (t_0)$, holds if and only if it holds in any fixed chart whose domain contains the foot.
Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch7-2-8-christoffel-transform \sketch Write $u_\beta =\tau \circ u_\alpha $ and use the first and second derivative chain rules together with section 1. The differentiability and geodesic-equation conditions therefore transfer between the two chart readings.

□
